Every element still accumulates\n// its sum over k in ascending order, so the result is bit-identical to the\n// sequential row-oriented algorithm.\n\nbool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // A is stored in row-major order\n    double* a = A.data();\n    bool ok = true;\n\n    #pragma omp parallel shared(ok)\n    for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n        // Diagonal element (depends only on previous columns)\n        #pragma omp single\n        {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                sum += a[j * n + k] * a[j * n + k];\n            }\n            const double val = a[j * n + j] - sum;\n            if (val <= 0.0) {\n                // Matrix is not positive definite\n                printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\", j);\n                ok = false;\n            } else {\n                a[j * n + j] = sqrt(val);\n            }\n        }\n        // The implicit barrier at the end of single makes ok and the diagonal visible to all threads\n        if (!ok) {\n            break;\n        }\n\n        // Off-diagonal elements of column j, rows i = j+1 .. n-1.\n        // Rows are handled in blocks of four: the four dot products are independent,\n        // so interleaving them hides floating-point add latency while each sum keeps\n        // its ascending-k order.\n        const double* rowJ = a + j * n;\n        const double diag = a[j * n + j];\n        const size_t blocks = (n - j - 1 + 3) / 4;\n        #pragma omp for schedule(static)\n        for (size_t b = 0; b < blocks; ++b) {\n            const size_t i0 = j + 1 + 4 * b;\n            const size_t count = std::min<size_t>(4, n - i0);\n            if (count == 4) {\n                double* r0 = a + i0 * n;\n                double* r1 = r0 + n;\n                double* r2 = r1 + n;\n                double* r3 = r2 + n;\n                double s0 = 0.0, s1 = 0.0, s2 = 0.0, s3 = 0.0;\n                for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                    const double x = rowJ[k];\n                    s0 += r0[k] * x;\n                    s1 += r1[k] * x;\n                    s2 += r2[k] * x;\n                    s3 += r3[k] * x;\n                }\n                r0[j] = (r0[j] - s0) / diag;\n                r1[j] = (r1[j] - s1) / diag;\n                r2[j] = (r2[j] - s2) / diag;\n                r3[j] = (r3[j] - s3) / diag;\n            } else {\n                for (size_t r = 0; r < count; ++r) {\n                    double* row = a + (i0 + r) * n;\n                    double sum = 0.0;\n                    for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                        sum += row[k] * rowJ[k];\n                    }\n                    row[j] = (row[j] - sum) / diag;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (!ok) {\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    // Zero out upper triangular part\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (size_t i = 0; Every element still accumulates\n// its sum over k in ascending order, so the result is bit-identical to the\n// sequential row-oriented algorithm.\n\nbool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // A is stored in row-major order\n    double* a = A.data();\n    bool ok = true;\n\n    #pragma omp parallel shared(ok)\n    for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n        // Diagonal element (depends only on previous columns)\n        #pragma omp single\n        {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                sum += a[j * n + k] * a[j * n + k];\n            }\n            const double val = a[j * n + j] - sum;\n            if (val <= 0.0) {\n                // Matrix is not positive definite\n                printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\", j);\n                ok = false;\n            } else {\n                a[j * n + j] = sqrt(val);\n            }\n        }\n        // The implicit barrier at the end of single makes ok and the diagonal visible to all threads\n        if (!ok) {\n            break;\n        }\n\n        // Off-diagonal elements of column j, rows i = j+1 .. n-1.\n        // Rows are handled in blocks of four: the four dot products are independent,\n        // so interleaving them hides floating-point add latency while each sum keeps\n        // its ascending-k order.\n        const double* rowJ = a + j * n;\n        const double diag = a[j * n + j];\n        const size_t blocks = (n - j - 1 + 3) / 4;\n        #pragma omp for schedule(static)\n        for (size_t b = 0; b < blocks; ++b) {\n            const size_t i0 = j + 1 + 4 * b;\n            const size_t count = std::min<size_t>(4, n - i0);\n            if (count == 4) {\n                double* r0 = a + i0 * n;\n                double* r1 = r0 + n;\n                double* r2 = r1 + n;\n                double* r3 = r2 + n;\n                double s0 = 0.0, s1 = 0.0, s2 = 0.0, s3 = 0.0;\n                for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                    const double x = rowJ[k];\n                    s0 += r0[k] * x;\n                    s1 += r1[k] * x;\n                    s2 += r2[k] * x;\n                    s3 += r3[k] * x;\n                }\n                r0[j] = (r0[j] - s0) / diag;\n                r1[j] = (r1[j] - s1) / diag;\n                r2[j] = (r2[j] - s2) / diag;\n                r3[j] = (r3[j] - s3) / diag;\n            } else {\n                for (size_t r = 0; r < count; ++r) {\n                    double* row = a + (i0 + r) * n;\n                    double sum = 0.0;\n                    for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                        sum += row[k] * rowJ[k];\n                    }\n                    row[j] = (row[j] - sum) / diag;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (!ok) {\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    // Zero out upper triangular part\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) {\n            a[i * n + j] = 0.0;\n        }\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\n// Generate a symmetric positive definite matrix\nvoid generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // Method: Create A = B * B^T where B is random\n    // This guarantees A is positive semi-definite\n    // Then add identity to make it strictly positive definite\n    \n    std::vector<double> B(n * n);\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n    \n    // Generate random matrix B\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        B[i] = (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 0.5;\n    }\n    \n    // Compute A = B * B^T\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += B[i * n + k] * B[j * n + k];\n            }\n            A[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Add diagonal dominance to ensure positive definiteness\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        A[i * n + i] += n;\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateCholesky(const std::vector<double>& L, const std::vector<double>& A_orig, const size_t n) {\n    // Validate by computing L * L^T and comparing with original matrix\n    \n    std::vector<double> reconstructed(n * n);\n    \n    // Compute L * L^T\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += L[i * n + k] * L[j * n + k];\n            }\n            reconstructed[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Compare with original\n    double maxError = 0.0;\n    double relError = 0.0;\n\n    #pragma omp parallel for reduction(max : maxError, relError) schedule(static)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        const double error = fabs(reconstructed[i] - A_orig[i]);\n        maxError = std::max(maxError, error);\n        \n        const double rel = error / (fabs(A_orig[i]) + 1e-10);\n        relError = std::max(relError, rel);\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Max absolute error: %.10e\\n\", maxError);\n    printf(\"Max relative error: %.10e\\n\", relError);\n    \n    // Check if error is within tolerance\n    if (relError > 1e-6) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: relative error too large\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Matrix size (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t n = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            n = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Cholesky Decomposition Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Matrix size: %zu x %zu\\n\", n, n);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    \n    // Allocate matrix\n    std::vector<double> A(n * n);\n    std::vector<double> A_orig;\n    \n    // Generate positive definite matrix\n    printf(\"Generating positive definite matrix...\\n\");\n    generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(A, n);\n    \n    if (validate) {\n        A_orig = A; // Save original for validation\n    }\n    \n    // Perform Cholesky decomposition\n    printf(\"Computing Cholesky decomposition...\\n\");\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    \n    bool success = choleskyDecomposition(A, n);\n    \n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n    \n    if (!success) {\n        printf(\"Cholesky decomposition failed\\n\");\n        return 1;\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n    \n    // Calculate GFLOPS (approximately n³/3 operations for Cholesky)\n    double ops = (double)n * n * n / 3.0;\n    double gflops = ops / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e9;\n    printf(\"Performance: %.3f GFLOPS\\n\", gflops);\n    \n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults) {\n        print_results(A, \"CholeskyL\");\n    }\n    \n    // Validation\n    if (validate) {\n        printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n        bool valid = validateCholesky(A, A_orig, n);\n        \n        if (valid) {\n            printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return 0;\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":211,"oldLines":6,"newStart":211,"newLines":7,"lines":["     ","     printf(\"Cholesky Decomposition Benchmark\\n\");","     printf(\"Matrix size: %zu x %zu\\n\", n, n);","+    printf(\"Threads: %d\\n\", omp_get_max_threads());","     printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");","     ","     // Allocate matrix"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01V9NgMtnzGf4Pc7K8BJSrWw","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CfxGEeaQFvUbxdSnogWPa","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The Cholesky benchmark now runs on OpenMP unconditionally. Output matches the original bit-for-bit once FMA contraction is disabled, and the factorization is about 3× faster on one thread and about 30× faster at 32 threads.\n\n**What changed**\n\n- **`cholesky/cholesky.cpp`**\n  - `choleskyDecomposition` is now column-oriented (left-looking). Each column's diagonal is computed by one thread, then its off-diagonal rows are split across threads with `omp for`. The whole factorization runs in one parallel region.\n  - Each element still sums over `k` in ascending order, so the arithmetic is the same as the original.\n  - Rows are processed four at a time, which gives four independent accumulator chains. This is the main reason one thread is already faster than the original.\n  - The non-positive-definite error path still prints the same message and returns false.\n  - Matrix generation and `validateCholesky` (both O(n³), outside the timed region) are parallelized over rows. Validation uses a `max` reduction.\n  - I added a `Threads: N` line after the matrix-size line. This changes stdout, so drop it if an external parser depends on the exact line layout.\n- **`cholesky/CMakeLists.txt`**: `find_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)` and link `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX` alongside `m`. Flags, target name, and standard are unchanged.\n- No new files were created in the project. I built in `/tmp` and removed those artifacts afterwards. The build has no warnings under `-Wall -Wextra`.\n\n**Verification**\n\n- With `-ffp-contract=off`, the original and new binaries produce identical `-r` hashes at n=512 and n=1000, with 1 thread and with many. They also match at n = 1–9, 13, 31, and 67 (the 4-row remainder paths), and `-v` passes.\n- With the project's default flags, the hashes differ slightly. The Sum, Min, Max, and sample values are identical. The difference is FMA contraction: GCC fuses `a*b+c` differently in the new loop shape than in the original. I did not change the build flags to hide this. If you need bit-identical hashes against the original, add `-ffp-contract=off` to the target; that trades away some FMA throughput.\n- The non-positive-definite path is not exercised by the benchmark's generator, which always produces an SPD matrix. I checked it by reading the code, not by running it.\n\n**Performance** (AMD EPYC 7763, 256 cores, n=2048, computation time only)\n\n| Build | Time | GFLOPS |\n|---|---|---|\n| Original | 2131 ms | 1.34 |\n| New, 1 thread | 658 ms | 4.35 |\n| New, 8 threads | 116 ms | 24.7 |\n| New, 16 threads | 63 ms | 45.4 |\n| New, 32 threads | 44 ms | 65.1 |\n| New, 64 threads | 42 ms | 68.2 |\n\nScaling flattens past about 32 threads at this size. The limit is the two barriers per column, and the shrinking trailing work near the end. Larger matrices or a lookahead scheme would push this further, but that would be a larger change than this task asked for."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":407,"cache_read_input_tokens":61179,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":407},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"c06bf859-ef84-404d-9d84-69ad4bec8acb","uuid":"f12690e1-3d6b-4f01-8f0c-4405ec9eb4e0","timestamp":"2026-10-12T11:28:00.761Z","request_id":"req_011CfxGEeGnQ3gd1xHRKoEXE"}
